question: Q-001
reason: The shell as built renders carol's ten links in the asserted order and grouping, and the geometry the scenario measures follows from the tokens. The sidebar grid column is var(--ui-sidebar-width), which tokens.css sets to 15rem, so the nav is 240 px wide and main, placed in column 2, starts at x 240. Each group is a p label followed by a ul named through aria-labelledby, group order is home, build, admin, more, and features register in file-name order, which gives Home, Flows, Runs, then Users, Roles and teams, Group mappings, Audit log, Tool servers, Grants, Policies. Exactly one nav is rendered because the same nav element is placed either in the header or after it. The unit's browser test asserts every item of the scenario, and it discriminates: design.md records that the base shell was a header list with a 297 px banner for carol, which fails assert_layout(page, 72) and the 240 px checks. The harness-generated test only errored at the merge base, which says nothing against the head.

question: Q-015
reason: The generated test only errored at the merge base, which says nothing against the head, and the shell gives the scenario. The Menu button is a plain Button with lg:hidden, aria-expanded bound to React state and aria-controls main-nav, so below 1024 px it is visible with aria-expanded false and from 1024 px it is display none. The sidebar nav is hidden when the state is closed and block when open, with lg:block from 1024 px, so a closed menu below 1024 px removes the navigation from the accessibility tree and the count is 0, while at 1024 px there is one navigation with id main-nav. A click toggles the state and an effect on the pathname closes it, so navigating from the not-found page to Home leaves aria-expanded false and no navigation. No Radix primitive is involved. The unit's own browser test, tagged with this criterion, asserts the button at 1023 and 1024, the two clicks at 900 with assert_layout and assert_accessible, the close on navigation and an empty CSP list.
